workflow_class: Gray pointer FIFO and cross-clock memory
rationale: Binary increment can change multiple bits, for example 0111 to 1000. Per-bit two-stage sampling can propagate an incoherent pointer into the explicitly stated read-side full/empty decisions.
caveats: This is a definite pointer-transfer defect, not a complete FIFO implementation. Reset, memory collisions, full/empty and wrap correctness remain unqualified; they neither repair nor negate the known crossing defect.

author_reading.evidence_and_limits: Binary pointer can change multiple bits; destination uses it for comparison. FIFO reset/memory behavior is intentionally unknown and must remain an additional unresolved scope.

labels.workflow_class: Gray pointer FIFO and cross-clock memory
labels.rationale: A binary pointer increment can toggle several bits, e.g. 0111 to 1000. Two stages independently capture those bits and cannot restore coherence. Read-side pointer decisions can therefore use a value that never existed.
labels.caveats: No full FIFO is present. Missing reset, memory and collision semantics independently block whole-FIFO acceptance but do not erase this definite pointer-transfer defect. No physical-skew or rate contract makes arbitrary binary transitions single-bit.

labels.workflow_class: Gray pointer FIFO and cross-clock memory
labels.rationale: A binary pointer increment can change several bits (0111 to 1000). Independently sampled first-stage bits can form a different pointer; the second stage preserves the incoherent value. Contract explicitly sends this value to full/empty logic, so two stages do not make this safe.
labels.caveats: FIFO reset, memory and collision behavior are genuinely unspecified. They block whole-FIFO acceptance but do not erase the known binary pointer defect. Sampling topology duplicates C09 except attributes; the source encoding premise is decisive.
